description: ODC: delete the WHOLE ENTITY, not its attributes. The ODC lane already proved deleting an attribute (delete-attribute-no-consumers, delete-data-consumers) and deleting logic (delete-logic-consumers), but no job took out of the model an entity that already existed. Here nothing is born: the model comes whole from the previous job through "base": "job:data-full-model", and this job only TOUCHES it - it deletes WfCovProject, the middle entity, leaving the root WfCovOrganization and the leaf WfCovTask standing. Three things that are only learned by doing. (a) Deleting an entity is a CHAIN, not an op: the FK WfCovTask.ProjectId is covered by two indexes, the author's and an AutoIndex_ProjectId that nobody wrote (in ODC each FK is born with its own index), and both have to go before the attribute, and the attribute before the entity. (b) The usages of an entity UNDER-REPORTS: a FK is not linked to the entity, it is linked to the IIdentifierType that is a CHILD of it, and the kernel discards referers that live inside the target - that is why op (2) says real=1 and does not name the FK that op (3) shows. Whoever forces looking only at that number breaks the model. (c) The delete of the entity IS REFUSED, and the refusal does not come from authoring: there is always left the anonymous Record type that the platform gives to every ODC entity. That Record cannot go first either - it is used by the entity actions of the entity itself and by its List type - so the circle has no entry and force is the only way. The job shows the two refusals in the _why of the ops (9) and proves that the force is legitimate in the only way that counts: it ends green, isValid=True and zero new messages in the Verify. What is left behind is in op (11).

ops.name: WfCovProject
ops._why: (1) BEFORE: the entity already exists when this job begins - it came from job:data-full-model, no op here creates it. Note that the find returns TWO objects with this name: the IServerEntity and a loose IAttribute. That second one is the clue to the rest of the job.

(2) BEFORE, the consumers of the entity: real=1, and it is no FK. It is IAnonymousStructure:WfCovProject Record/IAttribute:WfCovProject - the Record type that the platform gives to EVERY ODC entity and that points back to it. No authoring op can lower this number.

(3) and here is the trap of the number above: this attribute of ANOTHER entity has DataType '@<chave de WfCovProject>.#IdentifierType', that is, it links to the IIdentifierType that lives INSIDE WfCovProject. Since the kernel discards referers internal to the target (IsInside), the usages of op (2) never lists this FK: there is a whole dependency that the number hides. That is why the chain below is mandatory, and not a precaution.

(4) the FK attribute itself has real=2, and only one of them is the author's: IX_WfCovTask_ProjectDone (declared in the previous job) and AutoIndex_ProjectId, which no job wrote - in ODC each FK is born with its own index. The third referer, IRecordAttributeValue, is derived and does not block.

(5b) and the automatic index goes out: without it the attribute does not go out. It can be deleted like any other index, and deleting ONLY this one does not touch the sibling AutoIndex_PriorityId, which appears still standing in the dump of op (12).
(6) real=0: what remains is the IRecordAttributeValue of the sample record, derived (the same rule proven in delete-attribute-no-consumers.json)
(7) the FK goes out WITHOUT force: brokenConsumers=0. Only now has WfCovProject stopped having anything depending on it in authoring.
(8) AFTER taking out everything that was authoring, the number is the SAME as in op (2): real=1, the anonymous Record. This is the honest result - there is no sequence of ops that takes it to zero.

(9) THE REFUSAL and the way around it. Without force the kernel refuses with: delete: refused, IServerEntity 'WfCovProject' is used by 1 consumer(s): IAnonymousStructure:WfCovProject Record/IAttribute:WfCovProject (list them with usages, fix or remove those usages, or pass "force": true to break them). Taking that Record out first does not work either: delete: refused, IAnonymousStructure 'WfCovProject Record' is used by 6 consumer(s): IListType:WfCovProject Record List; IServerEntity:WfCovProject/IEntityActionSignature:UpdateWfCovProject/IInputParameterSignature:Source; ... GetWfCovProject/Record; CreateWfCovProject/Source; ... - that is, the Record is used by the entity actions and by the List type of the VERY entity that is to be deleted. The circle has no entry: force is the only way, and the legitimate one, because the only consumer it breaks is the pair that the platform maintains and that dies with the entity. The proof that it was legitimate is not in this _why, it is at the end of the job: brokenConsumers=1 and the Verify stays isValid=True with zero new messages.

ops.name: WfCovProject
ops._why: (10) AFTER: the entity disappeared from the module. What is left with this name is only the IAttribute of op (1) - the anonymous Record was left orphaned instead of going out with the entity.

(11) and that orphan is no longer used by anyone: real=0. The Verify does not flag it (it does not count among the UnusedElement of the author's structures), so in ODC the Record type of a deleted entity is silent garbage: whoever wants the module clean has to go and get it by hand, no message will remind them.

(12) read back the entity that REMAINED: without the attribute ProjectId, without IX_WfCovTask_ProjectDone, with AutoIndex_PriorityId still standing (only the automatic index of the deleted FK went out) and with the child IIdentifierType 'WfCovTask Identifier' visible - it is to this child that any FK links, the same mechanism that made the usages of op (2) under-report.

(13) and the root survives intact, with the same real=1 of its own anonymous Record: deleting the middle entity did not touch it, and the WfCovProject.OrganizationId that cited it went away together with the entity.
